MiniWireshark **5.3.4**: a medium release that makes MiniWireshark safer, easier to start and easier to understand.

**Security and privacy**
- Every finding of the 5.2.3 security audit is fixed in the code. Four of the fixes still need a check on real hardware (a Windows PC, a Mac, a real Wi-Fi roam).
- Linux and macOS no longer start as administrator. The password is asked for only when capture starts, and the demo and the help never ask.
- The data folder is closed to other users. Another user can no longer swap the compiled copy, the update rollback or the private packages.
- A new install no longer trusts its first network or starts Active Scanning by itself. "Session only" and "Delete ALL history" really delete.
- Passwords stay out of packet details, saved conversations, CSV files and copies. A new warning says when a login is sent without encryption, without keeping the password.
- A second device claiming to be the router raises a DANGER alert. The kill switch also stops package downloads.

**New**
- **Ready?** in the Welcome Center: what works, and a fix button for what doesn't.
- **Story mode** in the Timeline: what changed, day by day, in plain sentences.
- **Unusual activity** in the Security tab, with the worrying and the innocent reading side by side, and a day-and-night baseline for each device.
- **Seven guided questions**, among them DNS, IPv6, "can't connect", "Wi-Fi or Internet?" and call problems.
- **Calls**: loss and jitter of video and voice calls, from packet headers only.
- **Network check-up**: one plain-English page to print or send, names hidden by default.
- Alert snooze, your own blocklist, opt-in notifications while minimised, `--help` and `--version`, and a filter said in words.

**Speed and fixes**
- Windows now starts from the saved compiled copy too: on a Windows PC the first start went from about 14 to under 5 seconds, and memory from about 440 to about 220 MB.
- Packets are analysed about a fifth faster, and every list the analysis keeps now has a limit. Memory can still rise in a long, very busy capture (see Known limits).
- Damaged files, clocks that jump, and German and Windows 11 24H2 Wi-Fi output are handled. Layouts from 1024×768 up were checked in English, French and Spanish; Extra large text on a small screen is still cramped (see Known limits).

**Known limits**
- **Changing the text size on Windows is slow:** about 0.4 seconds, and the window doesn't answer for about a tenth of a second (the goal is 0.1 seconds). Making it fast needs a change to how the window shares its fonts, planned for a later release.
- **Not re-tested on a real PC for this release:** memory, threads and handles over an 8-hour capture on Windows, and the network-card pick with a VPN switched on. The fixes for the growth seen on an older build are checked by automated tests and replays only. Our own 30-hour replay of the analysis levels off after hour 24.
- **An upgrade from 5.3.3 or older turns the daily update check on**, even if it was off. A one-time notice says how to turn it off again.
- **A rollback can bring back an older genuine version** when an update fails to start three times, even if the update fixed a security problem. Download the newer version again.
- **Memory can still rise in a long, very busy capture.** In our harshest test (the same busy capture replayed in a loop for 20 minutes on Linux) the window grew by a few hundred MB. Every list MiniWireshark keeps has a limit; the cause of the rest is still being looked for.
- **Extra large text on a small screen is cramped**, and some labels are cut short (some Alerts cells, mostly in Spanish and French). The full text is in the line or panel under the table.
- **Started as administrator (root) on Linux, the window uses about 270 MB more memory**, because a root start never uses the saved compiled copy.
- **Wi-Fi (802.11, radiotap) management frames, such as beacons, get only a rough label and no device address**; Wi-Fi data frames are decoded. `.gz` captures must be unpacked first.
- **Opening a capture file raises a "new device" alert for every device in it.** A few French and Spanish alert sentences may keep English words, and some labels can still be cut off in French in a small window.
- Two messages at start still wait for a click ("Administrator required" when the Windows prompt is refused, "Startup error" when the window can't open); both end the program.
- The full list is in the changelog.

**Quality**
- Self-test: 480 tests, on Python 3.8, 3.12 and 3.13, on Windows (3.12 and 3.14) and on macOS. A test that can't run on a machine is counted as skipped, not passed. On Linux with Python 3.12, scapy and psutil: 477 passed, 0 failed, 3 skipped for reasons of the test machine. Without scapy and psutil, 40 more are skipped. The README lists every setup we measured.
- GUI test: 95 steps, on Ubuntu 22.04 and 24.04 and on Windows.
- A million damaged packets in a row, 0 errors.
